failure_summary: A5a fails 3/3 because the harness itself orders the colour naming — compute.mjs SPANISH_OUTPUT_DIRECTIVE (buildPromptForCondition locale suffix) says ‘Refer to the two discs as **verde** (first player) and **gris** (second player)’, and all three runs duly say ‘verde’, which the dispatch rubric bans; secondarily the offered alias opp-key-square (spec c3r1) carries the board-false role text ‘a single square completing your opponent’s four-in-a-row line’ on truthBoard=decision (on 334 the c2r1-c5r1 line needs BOTH c2r1 and c3r1; occupying c3r1 completes nothing — it is the fork pivot), which run 0 echoed as ‘c3r1 … es la que cierra esa línea’ (A4 fail), while run 1 additionally inverted the engine’s own finalMovestring 33432 (prompt_confusion, production-fidelity run so not separable from gpt-5.4-mini capability).
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; run 2 null (not scored, not a pass). A1/A2/A6/G7a/G7b copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_2026-08-31T12-52-38Z_mechanical.json (all pass, 3/3). | A5 (3/3 fail): runs 0,1,2 all name the first player by colour (‘la jugada más fuerte del verde’, ‘le negabas a verde’ x2). Assembled PROMPT (Step 0b) contains no colour word at all (checked: Green/Gray/green/gray all absent) — the colour comes from the harness locale suffix, so this is model-independent. Voice is otherwise clean: 2nd-person voseo-compatible imperfect, no internal vocabulary (no ‘ventana’, ‘recurso perdido’, ‘histograma’, ‘contexto de apertura’). A5b applies (player 2 + opening) and PASSES 3/3: no defeatist line, all three frame column 3 as the tougher defense. | A4 run 0 fail: ‘dejó libre la casilla c3r1, que es la que cierra esa línea; además … c2r1 como el otro punto de remate’ presents the double threat as {c3r1,c2r1}. Board truth on 33432: Green occupies c3r1 and the two winning squares are c2r1 and c6r1 (visualize_board 33432 — ‘Major threats: col2 row1 (X) [GT], col6 row1 (X) [GT]’). c6r1 is never mentioned in run 0. | A3+A4+G1+G2+G4 run 1 fail: ‘le dejaste ocupar c2r1, y con eso armó una doble amenaza sobre c3r1 y c6r1’ swaps pivot and finishing square. visualize_board 33431 (opponent takes c2r1) shows ‘Major threats: col3 row1 (X) [GT]’ — a SINGLE threat, and c6r1 is not a threat at all; this also contradicts render_decision.finalMovestring=33432 (G4) and the L2 frame text ‘let the opponent occupy column 3’ (G1), and mis-names the conceded cell the guardrail demands (G2a). | Run 2 is the clean run: ‘dejaste que tu rival ocupara c3r1 … con dos remates a la vez en c2r1 y c6r1’ matches 33432 exactly. | A7 pass 3/3 (a: cause given, not outcome; b: every referent named in prose or wrapped; c: fork pivot c3r1 named in runs 0 and 2 and offered as opp-key-square — run 1 names it too, though in the wrong role, charged at A3/A4 not double-charged here; d: named idea + squares). | G3 pass: afterBest/afterPlayed omitted as tag-identical and nothing in any answer needed them; the fork is only visible on 33432, which is not an offered board at all, but the L2 frame states it in prose. | G5 pass: rendered board carries ‘Tactics: (no tactics)’ — no false threat-list entry; the defect is in an alias ROLE string, recorded as a counterexample. | G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard=false is board-true (3342 shows no major threats) and L2/realized_denied/enabled_opponent is the right route. | G7 pass 3/3: annotationRepairs empty on all runs, all five handles offered, line-words on opp-key-line and square-words on the single-square handles. | NOT charged, but report: guardDiagnostics on runs 1 and 2 shows ‘P5strong:cell_not_allowed:c6r1’ with strippedSpecs [c6r1] — the model listed c6r1 in key_cells though only c2r1/c3r1 were offered as cells, so the second winning square of the fork ships as UNHIGHLIGHTED prose. | NOT charged per v2 addendum, but a real es-locale defect: the guard humanizes cNrM into ENGLISH inside Spanish prose — served text reads ‘la casilla column 3, row 1’ and ‘le dejaste ocupar column 2, row 1’ (reasonRenderGuard stripInternalTokens is not localized).

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: compute.mjs SPANISH_OUTPUT_DIRECTIVE (locale suffix appended by buildPromptForCondition)
counterexamples.evidence: The directive orders ‘Refer to the two discs as verde (first player) and gris (second player)’; the assembled grounded PROMPT contains no colour word (Green/Gray/green/gray all absent), so all 3/3 ‘verde’ mentions are prompt-commanded, and they collide head-on with A5a’s ban on naming players by colour.

Role text calls c3r1 ‘a single square completing your opponent’s four-in-a-row line’, but on the decision board 334 the window c2r1-c5r1 holds only c4r1,c5r1 for Green, so it needs BOTH c2r1 and c3r1; c3r1 is the fork PIVOT (visualize_board 33432: Green plays c3r1, only then are c2r1 and c6r1 winning squares). Run 0 echoed the role verbatim and told the player c3r1 closes the line.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: opponentPunishment.entryCell / tie.sharedCells vs opponentPunishment.cells — no rendered field says WHICH cell the opponent occupies to create the fork
counterexamples.evidence: The internal JSON gives cells [c2r1,c6r1], completingCell c2r1, entryCell c2r1 and tie.sharedCells [c3r1]; run 1 read entryCell/completingCell c2r1 as the occupied square and produced ‘le dejaste ocupar c2r1 … doble amenaza sobre c3r1 y c6r1’, which visualize_board 33431 refutes (single threat col3 row1, c6r1 not a threat) and finalMovestring 33432 contradicts.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: zones.aliases offers no handle for c6r1 (the fork’s second winning square)
counterexamples.evidence: guardDiagnostics runs 1 and 2: failures [P5strong:cell_not_allowed:c6r1], strippedSpecs [c6r1] — c6r1 is in opponentPunishment.cells and anchorCells but was never offered, so the square that makes the threat a DOUBLE one can never be highlighted.
